Looking at the verification task, I need to analyze the lemma `Prove` in both `HelperA.dfy` and `HelperB.dfy`.

The lemma proves that `K.Compress(s) == s` when `K.Clean(s)` holds. Let me trace through the logic:

1. When `|s| < 2`: `O.Base(s)` establishes `K.Compress(s) == s`
2. When `|s| >= 2`:
   - We need to show `K.Clean(s[1..])` before recursively calling `Prove(s[1..])`
   - `O.TailInvariant(s)` provides that `K.Clean(s[1..])` when `K.Clean(s)` and `2 <= |s|`
   - `O.Boundary(s)` proves `s[0] != s[1]` when `K.Clean(s)` and `2 <= |s|`
   - `O.Keep(s)` proves `K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + K.Compress(s[1..])` when `2 <= |s|` and `s[0] != s[1]`
   - After the recursive call, we know `K.Compress(s[1..]) == s[1..]`
   - So `K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + s[1..] == s`

The issue is that before calling `Prove(s[1..])` recursively, we need to establish its precondition `K.Clean(s[1..])`. This requires calling `O.TailInvariant(s)` before the recursive call.

Let me construct the correct proof body:

```dafny
if |s| < 2 {
  O.Base(s);
} else {
  O.TailInvariant(s);  // establishes K.Clean(s[1..])
  Prove(s[1..]);       // recursive call, now precondition is satisfied
  O.Boundary(s);       // establishes s[0] != s[1]
  O.Keep(s);           // establishes K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + K.Compress(s[1..])
  assert s == [s[0]] + s[1..];
}
```
